paper.title: LAPS: Automating Hypothesis-Driven Statistical Analysis of Public Survey Using Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Public surveys are indispensable resources for understanding social dynamics, yet their analysis often imposes a high cognitive load due to structural complexity. In this paper, we present LAPS, a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted automated framework that supports end-to-end, hypothesis-driven statistical analysis of survey data. LAPS consists of four modules (i.e., Operationalization, Planning, Execution, and Reporting) with human-in-the-loop mechanisms to balance automation with user agency. To evaluate the applicability of LAPS, we conducted a within-subjects user study with 12 social science researchers across three analytical environments: traditional statistical tools, a general-purpose LLM, and LAPS. Our findings demonstrate that LAPS ensures researcher agency and analytical stability, reduces the cognitive burden in the analysis workflow, and produces trustworthy, coherent outputs. Based on these findings, we reflect on how LAPS improves researchers’ workflows and discuss design implications for scalable and trustworthy human-AI collaboration in survey-based research.

system.name: Tree-of-Analysis
system.description: Tree-of-Analysis (ToA) supports conversational exploration of tabular data by automatically organizing AI-generated charts and explanations into an interactive analysis tree. It identifies analytical triggers, recommends contextual follow-up questions, and lets users navigate or filter previous analysis steps.

Chart-based tree connections use deterministic rules, whereas text-only clarify and contextualize connections use LLM-based semantic matching. The processes illustrate connected interaction paths; subsequent analysis turns repeat the relevant tree-construction and recommendation steps.

The model then selects three promising triggers using the analysis context, predicts suitable follow-up analysis targets, and generates three recommended questions. paper.title: QuerySwitch: Supporting the Design Process by Balancing Vagueness through Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Designers often regard vagueness as an essential aspect of creative work, as it fosters diverse interpretations and helps prevent fixation. Although large language models (LLMs) are increasingly viewed as a promising creative partner, designers struggle to productively incorporate vagueness into AI-supported workflows. To address this challenge, we present QuerySwitch, an interactive prototype that enables fashion designers to manage vagueness by flexibly switching between two distinct query-output modes. Findings from a user study show that QuerySwitch helps fashion designers balance vagueness, enhances the usability of LLMs in design tasks, and promotes creative exploration. This work contributes to HCI by (1) foregrounding a critical construct in human–AI collaboration, (2) demonstrating how interaction mechanisms can scaffold designer agency in LLMs use, and (3) articulating design principles—structuring exploration and preserving key query formulations—that extend to creativity-driven domains.

system.processScope: The interactive fashion design workflow, covering abstract concept exploration, moodboard image generation, moodboard-based sketch exploration, and fashion design image generation. The two sketch parallel-query configurations are represented as alternative processes.

Human completion is therefore represented at a high level. Image storage and REST transmission are treated as implementation details within prompt construction rather than separate processes.

paper.title: InfoAlign: A Human–AI Co-Creation System for Storytelling with Infographics
paper.abstract: Storytelling infographics are a powerful medium for communicating data-driven stories through visual presentation. However, existing authoring tools lack support for maintaining story consistency and aligning with users’ story goals throughout the design process. To address this gap, we conducted formative interviews and a quantitative analysis to identify design needs and common story-informed layout patterns in infographics. Based on these insights, we propose a narrative-centric workflow for infographic creation consisting of three phases: story construction, visual encoding, and spatial composition. Building on this workflow, we developed InfoAlign, a human–AI co-creation system that transforms long or unstructured text into stories, recommends semantically aligned visual designs, and generates layout blueprints. Users can intervene and refine the design at any stage, ensuring their intent is preserved and the infographic creation process remains transparent. Evaluations show that InfoAlign preserves story coherence across authoring stages and effectively supports human–AI co-creation for storytelling infographic design.

paper.title: DataSpeck: An AI-Driven Human-in-the-Loop System for Automating Transformations in Data Conversion Workflows
paper.abstract: In data-driven systems, integrating disparate data sources becomes challenging when incoming data does not conform to the system’s specifications. Despite advances in automated schema matching systems, data integration tasks involving complex semantic interrelationships still require users to manually identify and define transformations between datasets, which can be cognitively demanding and time-consuming. We present DataSpeck, an end-to-end system that automates the conversion of disparate data sources to fit any pre-existing data specification. DataSpeck employs an AI-driven human-in-the-loop design, using LLMs to analyze semantic relationships and generate step-by-step transformation pipelines autonomously, while only requesting user attention to resolve semantic ambiguities. In our technical evaluation, DataSpeck successfully automated ~86% of varied data transformations while generating interpretable strategies with confidence scores and targeted clarification requests. In a user study (N=12), participants completed data conversion tasks ~53% faster with significantly reduced cognitive load using DataSpeck compared to Microsoft Excel with Copilot.

system.name: DataSpeck
system.description: DataSpeck automatically converts source datasets into a target dataset specification by using LLMs to infer semantic relationships, generate transformation strategies, and produce executable Python pipelines. Users resolve ambiguities through targeted clarifications and can inspect and revise individual pipeline steps through natural language.
system.processScope: End-to-end data conversion, including descriptor analysis, semantic relationship inference, confidence-based human clarification, stepwise code generation and execution, pipeline refinement, error recovery, and optional row-wise LLM transformations.
system.notes: The paper does not fully specify the scheduling of descriptor and strategy regeneration after every possible combination of user clarifications. The clarification processes represent the supported recalculation paths without assuming additional orchestration behavior.

GPT-4o generates Python transformation steps with descriptions and completion indicators, and the code executor runs each step to produce intermediate outputs. Generation and execution repeat until the model determines that the target specification has been satisfied, producing the complete pipeline code and converted dataset. A separate pipeline is generated for each target table.

paper.title: Virtual Minds, Real Work: LLM-Powered Preference-Based Planning through Spatial Multi-Agent-Human Collaboration
paper.abstract: People frequently face preference-based planning tasks requiring balancing goals with nuanced constraints, yet even advanced LLMs demand considerable effort to produce and adjust plans reflecting complex user preferences. We present MAVIS (Multi-Agent Virtual Interactive Synergy), a multi-agent system within a virtual workspace that introduces an incremental collaboration mechanism. This mechanism automatically decomposes tasks into guidelines and sequentially introduces expert agents. Each agent proactively engages users in focused dialog to uncover implicit preferences, while successive agents add perspectives and transparently negotiate trade-offs. To mitigate textual overload, MAVIS employs spatial visualizations that externalize agents’ reasoning through step-linked summaries and context-aware boards, with embodied avatars supporting natural interaction. Across studies, Study 1 showed our collaboration mechanism doubled expressed preferences and improved planning quality by 60.3% over a conventional LLM baseline. Study 2 affirmed visualization’s benefits over a non-spatial baseline, while Study 3 confirmed its versatility across VR and desktop modalities and diverse tasks.

Users approve an automatically generated collaboration guideline, discuss preferences with specialized agents, steer negotiations, and export a consolidated plan.

system.notes: The editable configuration path is shown; users can also approve the original guideline without edits. Specialist agents are generated for the task, so the two specialists shown in negotiation represent one exchange, not a fixed agent roster. paper.title: Human-AI Interaction for Time-Critical Sensemaking in Missing Persons Investigations
paper.abstract: Every year an estimated 200,000 people go missing in the UK alone. Missing persons investigations involve challenging time-critical sensemaking tasks based on fragmented data sources. This paper describes a mixed-methods participatory study evaluating data science and AI-driven techniques (summarisation, fact extraction, and data visualisation) for supporting these investigations as part of a human-centered workflow. A series of human-AI interfaces were iteratively designed and tested with search officers and domain experts at Police Scotland. Based on findings, we describe: (1) user and information needs for missing persons investigations; (2) insights on the benefits and challenges of applying LLM-based techniques in high-risk contexts; and (3) lessons for integrating AI for sensemaking tasks in policing more broadly. We highlight that in high-stakes contexts, where accuracy and context-sensitivity are paramount, AI techniques must be balanced with other approaches and designed in close partnership with end-users.

paper.title: Req2CAD: bridging functional requirements and parametric CAD models to support conceptual 3D design
paper.abstract: Conceptual CAD requires transforming functional requirements into parametric 3D models, yet existing systems have steep learning curves and limit creativity through premature fixation. Generative AI shows promise in producing diverse alternatives, while current methods mainly reconstruct CAD modeling sequences of existing designs, making them unsuitable for early stages where ideas are vague and intent is difficult to express. We present Req2CAD, an interactive system that enables designers to progress from design problems toward conceptual CAD models through functional decomposition, function–structure reasoning, and component-level CAD creation and iteration. Req2CAD introduces a data annotation pipeline that maps functional requirements to the 3D structural design space, a dual-feature CAD representation to support design space exploration and CAD ideation, and a progressive CAD generation method that enables rapid CAD model creation through multi-modal intent expression. A technical evaluation and user study demonstrate the effectiveness of Req2CAD, highlighting its potential for human–AI co-creation.

system.name: Req2CAD
system.description: Req2CAD supports conceptual 3D design by decomposing functional requirements, recommending and organizing relevant CAD components, and helping designers generate or edit parametric CAD models. Designers can explore structural alternatives, incrementally generate CADQuery code using text and graphical face selection, edit component geometry, inspect potential fusion regions, and export components for assembly.
system.processScope: Includes offline construction of the function–structure knowledge base and the interactive workflow from design problem specification through function decomposition, CAD case exploration, component editing, progressive generation, fusion guidance, and export for assembly.
system.notes: Fusion-anchor detection identifies potentially corresponding regions but does not automatically fuse components. Final component assembly is performed by designers in external CAD software. The interaction processes represent connected example paths through optional modes; designers can skip editing, use either recommendation mode, and revisit earlier stages.

processes.name: Construct function-structure knowledge base
processes.description: Starting from the Text2CAD dataset, the Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct vision-language model infers possible functions from each component's multi-view images. The Qwen3-14B language model extracts verb-object function keywords, and the annotation pipeline filters indeterminate cases and builds a knowledge base linking functional descriptions and keywords to CAD components.

processes.name: Decompose design problem
processes.description: The designer enters a design problem and requests function decomposition. The GPT-4o language model generates basic sub-functions in verb-object form, and Req2CAD organizes them into a design flowchart with the target product as the parent node and sub-functions as child nodes.

processes.name: Revise functional decomposition
processes.description: After the function decomposition is displayed, the designer can edit existing sub-function nodes or add custom ones to refine the design flowchart. The revised functions become available for subsequent CAD case recommendations.

processes.name: Explore CAD cases for a single function
processes.description: The designer selects one sub-function from the flowchart and requests recommended components. The Qwen3-Embedding-4B text embedding model supports semantic matching against the function–structure knowledge base, from which the system randomly samples 50 relevant cases. B-rep topology and 3DShape2Vec geometry features organize the cases into a similarity-based canvas, where the designer can inspect and select a case to add to the flowchart. The designer can request further random samples using the More button.

The system prioritizes components satisfying the greatest number of selected functions and displays up to 50 cases organized by geometric or topological similarity. The designer explores the clustered canvas and adds a selected component to the design flowchart.

processes.name: Edit retrieved CAD component
processes.description: The designer imports a recommended CAD component from the design flowchart into the graphical editor. Req2CAD extracts its original 2D sketch and extrusion parameters, which the designer can modify by dragging sketch points, changing extrusion distance, or editing numerical parameters. The editor updates the 3D component, which can then be recorded as an iterative node in the flowchart.

processes.name: Identify component fusion anchors
processes.description: The designer selects two CAD components from the design flowchart to investigate possible fusion. Req2CAD compares their 2D sketch graphs and uses 3DShape2Vec point cloud features to detect similar local regions, then highlights candidate fusion anchors. The designer can inspect alternative matched regions and use them as guidance for subsequent component editing or generation.

processes.name: Generate initial CAD component
processes.description: After exploring structural references, the designer writes a description of the component to create, optionally drawing on prompts associated with recommended cases. The GPT-4o language model generates CADQuery Python code, which the designer can review before running with the CADQuery compiler. Req2CAD displays the resulting parametric 3D component and extracts its face-adjacency graph for later face-based modifications. The designer can add the generated component to the design flowchart.

processes.name: Progressively extend CAD component
processes.description: When the designer wants to add or change a structure, they select a target face using the B-rep graph and enter a local text instruction. Req2CAD resolves the selected face to its stable index, and the GPT-4o language model generates an incremental CADQuery code fragment conditioned on the existing code, instruction, and face index. The fragment is appended to the previous code and executed to produce the updated component and face graph. This process repeats until the designer is satisfied, with generated versions optionally added to the flowchart.

paper.title: Bridging Gulfs in UI Generation through Semantic Guidance
paper.abstract: While generative AI enables high-fidelity UI generation from text prompts, users struggle to articulate design intent and evaluate or refine results—creating gulfs of execution and evaluation. To understand the information needed for UI generation, we conducted a thematic analysis of UI prompting guidelines, identifying key design semantics and discovering that they are hierarchical and interdependent. Leveraging these findings, we developed a system that enables users to specify semantics, visualize relationships, and extract how semantics are reflected in generated UIs. By making semantics serve as an intermediate representation between human intent and AI output, our system bridges both gulfs by making requirements explicit and outcomes interpretable. A comparative user study suggests that our approach enhances users’ perceived control over intent expression and outcome interpretation, and facilitates more predictable iterative refinement. Our work demonstrates how explicit semantic representation enables systematic and explainable exploration of design possibilities in AI-driven UI design.

system.name: GenUI Tool
system.description: A semantic-based UI generation system that lets users express design intent through structured semantic fields or natural-language descriptions, generates React interfaces, and analyzes how design semantics are implemented. Users can inspect semantic relationships and refine individual requirements while preserving existing design decisions.
system.processScope: End-to-end specification, generation, analysis, and iterative refinement of a single React component.
system.notes: Natural-language and manual specification are alternative entry modes that populate the same application-level semantic state. Analysis and refinement operate on that state regardless of how it was initially created.

processes.name: Generate UI from natural-language intent
processes.description: The user describes the desired interface in natural language. GPT-5 parses the description into structured semantics across Product, Design System, Feature, and Component levels. The application compiles these semantics into a Markdown prompt, Vercel's v0-1.5-md generates React component code, and the application renders a live preview.

-> [tool_2 execute]
-> (semantics_1: instruction record) + (ui_code_1: artifact formal) + (ui_preview_1: artifact visual)

processes.name: Generate UI from manually specified semantics
processes.description: Instead of writing a free-form description, the user directly fills semantic fields in the four-level framework. The application converts the structured requirements into a Markdown prompt, v0-1.5-md generates React component code, and the application renders the resulting interface. Users can leave fields unspecified for the generation model to infer.

processes.name: Analyze semantic relationships before generation
processes.description: After specifying design requirements, the user can trigger relationship analysis before generating an interface. GPT-5 examines dependencies between semantic attributes, identifies matching values, conflicts, and missing values, and recommends compatible specifications. The application displays these relationships as a graph, and the user can select an attribute to inspect its influences and suggested values.

processes.name: Extract augmented semantics from generated UI
processes.description: After an interface is generated, the user can trigger Analyze. GPT-5 examines the generated React code and its rendered screenshot to extract implemented design semantics, including visual properties, structural decisions, and details inferred by the UI generation model. The system combines these findings with the original user-specified values and presents the additional semantics in the semantic panel.

processes.name: Analyze semantic relationships after generation
processes.description: After augmented semantics are extracted, the user can analyze relationships among the implemented design attributes. GPT-5 identifies compatible, conflicting, and incomplete semantic relationships, including connections between original requirements and inferred design choices. The application visualizes these relationships, and selecting an attribute reveals upstream influences, downstream effects, explanations, and suggested refinements.

processes.name: Refine semantics and regenerate UI
processes.description: After generating an interface, the user changes a semantic value directly or accepts a suggested refinement. The application compares the previous and updated semantics to construct an explicit semantic diff, then prepares a revision prompt containing the changed requirements and existing React code. Vercel's v0-1.5-md regenerates the component while being instructed to preserve unaffected structure, and the application renders the updated UI. This cycle repeats whenever the user makes further refinements.
